title: Load a strip of nails into a framing nailer: heads in the head track, past the nail stop, the pusher eased on
instruction: Load the strip of nails into the framing nailer. Feed it into the rear end of the magazine, front first with the nail heads in the head track, and push it in past the nail stop. Then slide the pusher all the way back past the strip and ease it forward against the nails without letting it snap.
context: Framers and other carpenters reload their nailers all day: a strip holds 25 nails. RIDGID, R350RHA 21-degree framing nailer operator's manual, Loading the tool with nails: "feed a strip of nails into the magazine. Be sure the nails are pointed downward and at the angle shown", "Slide the pusher all the way to the rear of the magazine. Release the pusher and allow it to push the nails up to the driving mechanism", "Do not allow the pusher to snap back into place". NIOSH 2011-202 (Nail Gun Safety): nail guns are "used every day on many construction jobs, especially in residential construction". Done by: carpenters (BLS, 889,700 jobs), framers in particular.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A red 21-degree pneumatic framing nailer, not connected to air, lies on its side, fixed; its aluminium magazine (34 cm) runs along y, its rear end at y 13, its track's middle line at x 17, 3.4 cm up, its nose and driver to the robot's right, its handle on the far side. The track: a 7.5 mm slot for the shanks and, on the far side, an 11.5 mm head track (the 7.1 mm heads don't fit the slot); 83 mm across; its entry edges chamfered; its last 55 mm open on top (the loading window), with a 32 mm wide, 15 mm deep pocket in that part of the floor; the nail stop 35 mm in. The pusher: a black slider on a rail beside the head track, its knob (12 x 14 x 16 mm) at (22.5, -18.5), 6 cm up, 25 mm behind its finger; a spring pulls it towards the driver (about 3 N there, 6 N at the rear); empty, its finger rests at the driver. The strip: 25 plastic-collated 21-degree full round head nails, 3 in x .131 in, 21.5 cm long, 7.6 cm across, 130 g, orange collation, lying flat on a 2x4 offcut (38 x 89 mm, 20 cm long, standing on edge, fixed) at (38.5, 26), along x, its front (the first nail's point) away from the arms, its heads to the robot's left. Both grippers start open at the ready pose.
scoring: From the magazine's model and the parts' poses. In the track: the strip's front inside the rear end, within 4 mm of the track's line and of lying on the slot's floor, within 10 degrees of its direction, heads towards the head track. Past the nail stop: its back more than 36 mm in. Snapped: the pusher met the strip, or pushed it short of the driver, faster than 0.25 m/s. Up to the driver: the first nail within 1 mm of it. 1.0: the strip up to the driver with the pusher against it, the pusher never having snapped, both grippers more than 2 cm from the strip and the pusher's knob, held 1 s (0.9 if time runs out first). 0.5: fed up to the driver, but the pusher snapped. 0.25: in the track the right way round and past the nail stop, not fed. 0: anything else, a strip in back to front included.
reset_notes: Pull the pusher back and lift the strip out through the loading window; let the pusher back to the driver; lay the strip on the offcut, front away from the arms, heads to the robot's left.
fidelity: The nailer is fixed, unplugged and never fires; the magazine is a model: a strip with its heads on the wrong side is stopped at the rear end, one past the nail stop is held there, the pusher's finger drags a strip it rides back over and drops in behind its last nail, then pushes it to the driver. The window's pocket lets fingertips push the strip's back; the strip is rigid, on an offcut so fingers fit under its edges.
